title: Secondhand Stress: How Stressful Disclosures Affect Psychosocial Wellbeing in Online Graduate Admissions Communities
abstract: arXiv:2610.22657v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Online communities provide spaces for individuals navigating stressful life transitions to disclose difficulties and seek peer support. Yet encountering others' distress may also have psychosocial implications for community members. Drawing on stress crossover theory, we examine how engagement with peer distress during graduate admissions is associated with subsequent psychosocial expression and participation, and whether similar associations extend through downstream interactions. We analyze 171,981 posts and 1,130,413 comments from two Reddit communities across three admissions cycles, using propensity-score stratification and baseline-adjusted comparisons. Users who engaged with distress disclosures during application preparation subsequently exhibited higher classifier-estimated anxiety, depression, and stress expression, alongside greater commenting activity and lexical redundancy. These associations recurred across admissions cycle

translated_title: 二手压力：压力性表露如何影响在线研究生申请社群中的心理社会福祉
translated_abstract: 在线社群为经历压力性生活转变的个人提供了倾诉困难和寻求同伴支持的空间。然而，接触他人的痛苦也可能对社群成员产生心理社会层面的影响。基于压力交叉理论，我们研究了在研究生申请过程中与同伴的痛苦表露进行互动，如何与后续的心理社会表达和参与行为相关联，以及类似的关联是否会通过下游互动延伸开来。我们分析了来自两个Reddit社群、跨越三个申请周期的171,981条帖子和1,130,413条评论，采用倾向得分分层和基线调整比较方法。结果显示，在申请准备阶段与痛苦表露互动的用户，随后表现出更高的、由分类器估计的焦虑、抑郁和压力表达，同时评论活动更为频繁、词汇冗余度更高。这些关联在各个申请周期中反复出现。
tldr: 基于压力交叉理论，本研究通过大规模分析Reddit研究生申请社群中的帖子与评论发现，与他人的压力表露进行互动的用户，后续会表现出更高的焦虑、抑郁和压力表达水平以及更活跃的参与行为。
en_tdlr: Drawing on stress crossover theory, this large-scale analysis of Reddit graduate admissions communities reveals that users who engage with peers' distress disclosures subsequently exhibit higher anxiety, depression, and stress expression alongside greater participation.
